Windows stage private memory is current process PrivateUsage sampled nominally every 20 ms while named stages are active. Values overlap across stages, include profiler overhead, miss short stages and between-sample peaks, and are not allocations attributable to a stage. Null means no successful sample; failed samples are counted. Other platforms have no stage private-memory sampling.

Stage I/O uses process-wide overlapping windows and includes profiling writes; it is not additive. Explicit attributed bytes/call elapsed/block durations cover only annotated operations; call elapsed includes scheduling and copying and is not blocked I/O. Failed calls can leave partial byte counts unknown. Windows peak_private is process lifetime peak committed private/pagefile usage; Linux private peak unavailable.
